name: Reith bei Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: Charming scattered village with farms and one of the most beautiful panoramic views of the Kitzbüheler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Reith bei Kitzbühel is situated in the Kitzbühel district at 762 metres above sea level in the sunny Leukental valley, home to around 1,770 residents. The municipality nestles along the gentle southern slopes of the Bichlach hilly landscape, nestled between the world-famous alpine sports town of Kitzbühel to the east and Kirchberg in the Brixental valley to the west. Reith is cherished as a tranquil, sun-blessed residential village in the immediate vicinity of Kitzbühel. The village boasts traditional timber-clad farmhouses, elegant country homes, and uninterrupted panoramas encompassing the rugged peaks of the Wilder Kaiser, the Kitzbüheler Horn, and the Hahnenkamm.

Geschichte

Reith was first documented in 1188 upon the consecration of its church as ecclesia de ruote in records of the Scheyern Monastery, with its name signifying forest clearance. From the 15th through the 18th centuries, the village flourished during a silver and copper mining boom at the nearby Rerobichl hill, whose mine shafts ranked among the deepest in Europe. Around 1460, Schloss Münichau castle was constructed as the aristocratic seat of the Lords of Münichau; their heraldic monk still graces the municipal coat of arms. The baroque parish church of St. Giles (St. Ägidius) was rebuilt starting in 1727 by Tyrolean master builder Abraham Millauer, featuring an imposing onion dome and ceiling frescoes created by Simon Benedikt Faistenberger in 1729.

Anreise

Reith bei Kitzbühel is easily accessible by car and public transport. Motorists arriving from Germany can travel vignette-free via the A93 motorway exit Kufstein-Süd, continuing along the B178 and B170 highways. From Salzburg or Vienna, access leads through Lofer and St. Johann in Tirol. Train passengers arrive at Kitzbühel main railway station (5 kilometres away) or Kirchberg in Tirol along the Salzburg-Tyrol railway line, both served by Intercity and Railjet express services. The local S-Bahn Tirol stops at the nearby Schwarzsee halt. Regular VVT regional buses 4002 and 4006 connect Kitzbühel to Reith in five to eight minutes.

Tipps

A natural sanctuary is the pristine Gieringer Weiher lake nestled in the Bichlach conservation area, featuring healing peaty moor waters, sunbathing lawns, and views of the Wilder Kaiser range. Golf enthusiasts enjoy the 18-hole championship layout at Golfclub Kitzbühel-Schwarzsee-Reith, renowned for hole 16, known as the Mausefalle, played across a steep ravine. In winter, cross-country skiers access groomed trails directly from the village, including the illuminated night track at the Kulturhaus. In addition, beginners and families can practise on the gentle Huberwiese ski slope in the village centre, while Lake Schwarzsee nearby offers boating and walking.
